title: Gen-CB
fill_note: DENSE layered wind with a jig; scorer cap 0.65
fill_how: The scored turns assume a dense, layer-by-layer wind at fill 0.65 (insulated-wire area / window; the scorer cap). Use a winding jig on a drill/lathe with a turn counter, lay each layer side-by-side with light back-tension, and do not scramble-wind: a scramble wind only reaches ≈0.55–0.60 and then the window holds fewer turns (scorer what-if `--fill 0.60` is in the table above). Never wind more than the listed turns — the copper must stay below the flanges.
steel_extra: **New steel:** Ø194 discs, M3 clamp map R30 at 0/90/180/270° and R44 on the inter-pole angles 67.5/112.5/247.5/292.5° (both inside the R84 magnet ring). Cut from this kit's `steel_backiron_disc.dxf`; no earlier disc fits.
o5_note: scan t6: diametric Ø5 assists lower this 8p/12c layout, so all 48 Ø5 are left out
card_title: Gen-CB · Gen-CA rotors · MIN-GAP wire-saver stator (≈300 m)
card_sub: same R84 arcs / hubs / Ø194 steel / bridges as Gen-CA · 12 bobbins r63–102 × 4.05 mm copper (gap 6.65 mm) · no Ø5 · 2026-10-13
idea: Wire-saver stator for the Gen-CA rotors: only 4.05 mm of copper (9 layers), so the magnet faces are 6.65 mm apart and peak Bz at the copper reaches ≈0.70 T. It needs ≈300 m of wire (≈80 m less than Gen-CA, ≈75 m less than Gen-BX) and still out-scores the Gen-BX champion; it shares every rotor part, the steel, the frame rods and the bearing bridges with Gen-CA, so the two stators swap on the same machine.
